newsitem.title: USA: AMR revenues dampened by strike, excise tax.
newsitem.headline: AMR revenues dampened by strike, excise tax.

text.p: AMR Corp., the parent of American Airlines, posted record second-quarter earnings, but said revenues were dampened by the return of the passenger excise tax and the pilot strike earlier this year.

AMR posted second-quarter net earnings of $302 million, or $3.26 per share, compared with $293 million, or $3.35 a share last year. Total operating revenues rose to $4.71 billion, from $4.55 billion a year ago.

"Although some residual losses resulting from the earlier threat of a pilot strike and the reimposition of the domestic excise tax adversely impacted our results, our year-over-year improvement reflects strong demand for summer air travel ... and some substantive improvement in our operating performance," AMR Chairman Robert Crandall said in a statement.
AMR did not comment on the specific impact of the strike and excise tax.

As part of contentious labour negotiations earlier this year, American Airlines pilots went on strike Feb. 15, but were sent back to work within minutes by a presidential emergency board established to resolve the dispute.

Although the pilots' strike was short-lived, passengers had already booked flights on other airlines to avoid being stranded. American had previously said the labour disruptions cut first-quarter earnings by $70 million.
In addition to the strike, American also felt the effects of the return of the passenger excise tax in March.

The 10 percent tax was not in effect during last year's second quarter, which gave American and all airlines a cash windfall that normally goes to the Federal Aviation Administration and inflated year-ago revenues.
Separately, American Airlines said its second-quarter passenger load factor was 70.5 percent, up from 69.4 percent a year ago.

Second-quarter operating expenses per available seat-mile increased to 9.15 cents, from 8.84 cents a year ago. Passenger revenue per available seat-mile was 9.40 cents, compared with 9.13 cents last year.
AMR stock rose $4.94 to $100 a share on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.
